name: UDIAT / Dataset B
full_name: Breast Ultrasound Dataset B
paper_title: Automated Breast Ultrasound Lesions Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
paper_venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
notes: Images are from different women and may contain one or more lesions. The paper reports lesion delineations by experienced radiologists. The dataset is available through an application-based research-use workflow.

name: OASBUD
full_name: Open Access Series of Breast Ultrasonic Data
paper_title: Open access database of raw ultrasonic signals acquired from malignant and benign breast lesions
notes: Each lesion has two orthogonal RF acquisitions with paired binary ROI masks. B-mode images are not stored directly but can be generated from the RF echoes. Malignant lesions were histologically assessed by core-needle biopsy; some benign lesions were histologically assessed and the remainder were followed for two years. The two acquisitions from the same lesion should remain together when creating data splits.

name: Medical Image Database
full_name: Medical Image Database
paper_title: Automatic initialization of active contours and level set method in ultrasound images of breast abnormalities
notes: The associated paper evaluates 180 images from 180 patients and uses 15 additional database images for parameter tuning. The live website contains additional ultrasound, Doppler, elastography, and ground-truth entries, but its catalog includes repeated or incompletely described records; therefore, the structured scale above follows the clearly defined paper cohort. The website delivers ground truth primarily as contour-overlaid images rather than a clearly documented bulk archive of binary masks.

name: STU-Hospital
full_name: STU-Hospital
paper_title: An RDAU-NET model for lesion segmentation in breast ultrasound images
notes: STU-Hospital is the public repository name rather than a formal dataset name defined in the paper. The 42 images constitute an external test subset of the paper's larger test cohort. The released masks are grayscale expert-aggregation masks rather than consistently binary masks, and many mask dimensions differ from the released 128 x 128 ultrasound images. The repository does not provide patient-level metadata, per-image benign/malignant labels, a formal dataset license, or official preprocessing instructions.

name: BUSI
full_name: Dataset of Breast Ultrasound Images
paper_title: Dataset of breast ultrasound images
notes: The dataset contains 780 images from 600 women. The widely used released-file distribution is 133 normal, 437 benign, and 210 malignant images. The original Data in Brief article contains an internal inconsistency in its class-count table, so the released-file distribution is used here. The Mendeley record 10.17632/k8t3gnx9h6.1 is a later supplementary resource about BUSI data issues and is not treated as the original BUSI dataset source.

name: Breast lesion ultrasound video dataset
full_name: Breast lesion ultrasound video dataset
paper_title: A New Dataset and a Baseline Model for Breast Lesion Detection in Ultrasound Videos
paper_venue: Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention (MICCAI)
notes: The original paper does not assign a formal dataset name; BUSV, BUV, and BreastVid are aliases used in later literature or catalogs. The repository distributes extracted PNG frames grouped by video rather than conventional encoded video files. A 2023 repository correction identifies one duplicated/wrongly labelled video and four same-patient videos requiring label correction; revised global totals were not explicitly reported, so the scale and class distribution above retain the paper-reported values with this caveat.

name: Breast Ultrasound Image Database
full_name: Breast Ultrasound Image Database
paper_title: An open-access breast lesion ultrasound image database: Applicable in artificial intelligence studies
notes: The dataset contains 232 breast lesions, including 109 benign and 123 malignant lesions. Each lesion is represented by an original ultrasound image together with lesion-related annotation files on the official site. Patient-level identifiers, an official train/validation/test split, and a formal dataset license are not provided. The paper lists fine-needle aspiration, core-needle biopsy, and open biopsy among the reference methods; therefore, the broad label "histopathologically proven" should be interpreted with caution because fine-needle aspiration is cytologic sampling.

name: BUS-BRA
full_name: BUS-BRA: A Breast Ultrasound Dataset for Assessing Computer-aided Diagnosis Systems
paper_title: BUS-BRA: A breast ultrasound dataset for assessing computer-aided diagnosis systems
notes: All images have corresponding lesion masks, and the released metadata also provide bounding boxes, pathology, histology, BI-RADS categories, and standardized 5-fold and 10-fold cross-validation partitions. Patient-level pathology counts are 722 benign and 342 malignant, whereas image-level counts are 1,268 benign and 607 malignant. One released bounding box does not exactly match its corresponding mask extent. The outer cross-validation folds keep images from the same patient together, while the separate inner-validation flags should be regenerated if fully patient-disjoint validation is required.

name: BUSI_WHU
full_name: BUSI_WHU: Breast Cancer Ultrasound Image Dataset
notes: Version 3 contains 927 image-mask pairs. The patient_index field identifies 816 patients; image-level class counts are 560 benign and 367 malignant, while patient-level counts are 560 benign and 256 malignant. The release provides patient-linked morphology and size measurements but does not document the annotation procedure, diagnostic reference standard, or an official train/validation/test split. No dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper was identified, so the Mendeley Data DOI is recorded only under the data block and paper is set to null.

name: TDSC-ABUS2023
full_name: Tumor Detection, Segmentation and Classification Challenge on Automated 3D Breast Ultrasound 2023
paper_title: Tumor Detection, Segmentation and Classification Challenge on Automated 3D Breast Ultrasound: The TDSC-ABUS Challenge
notes: The dataset contains 200 tumor-containing 3D ABUS cases. The official split is 100 training, 30 validation, and 70 test cases. The training data include NRRD volumes, voxel-level tumor masks, and benign/malignant labels. Access requires a signed agreement and organizer approval, so file-level verification was not performed.

name: BUS_UC
full_name: BUS_UC Breast Ultrasound Dataset
paper_title: Memory-efficient transformer network with feature fusion for breast tumor segmentation and classification task
notes: The release contains 811 image-mask pairs, comprising 358 benign and 453 malignant images. The Mendeley page states that the source images were obtained from Ultrasound Cases and were subsequently annotated by an experienced radiologist. Patient identifiers, patient count, acquisition device, diagnostic reference standard, and an official split are not reported. One checked public mirror contains a one-pixel image-mask dimension mismatch for file 0319.png.

name: BUS-UCLM
full_name: BUS-UCLM: Breast Ultrasound Lesion Segmentation Dataset
paper_title: BUS-UCLM: Breast ultrasound lesion segmentation dataset
notes: The dataset contains 683 images from 38 patients: 419 normal, 174 benign, and 90 malignant. Some released images contain Doppler information; the public metadata identify 37 Doppler-marked records. Version 3 is licensed under CC BY 4.0, whereas version 1 used CC BY-NC 3.0. The public v3 PNG files have dimensions of 856 x 606, while the paper reports 768 x 1024; this discrepancy remains unresolved. Normal images have all-background masks.

name: US3M
full_name: Multimodal Breast Ultrasound Dataset US3M
paper_title: TDF-Net: Trusted Dynamic Feature Fusion Network for breast cancer diagnosis using incomplete multimodal ultrasound
notes: All 248 released patient folders contain all three ultrasound modalities. Missing modalities in the TDF-Net study are simulated experimentally rather than intrinsically absent from the public dataset. The release contains no segmentation masks, clinical-variable table, or official train/validation/test split.

name: ALN-Ultra
full_name: Early-stage Breast Cancer Ultrasound Dataset with Paired Images and Videos for Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis Prediction
notes: ALN-Ultra is described as paired ultrasound image/video data from 257 patients with early-stage breast cancer for axillary lymph node metastasis prediction. The current Zenodo replacement record is publicly visible, but its files are restricted. Exact image and video counts, file formats, detailed label schema, and official splits therefore cannot currently be verified. The original 2025 Zenodo record was 10.5281/zenodo.15003119. The current live replacement page does not display an explicit license value in its Rights section, so the license is recorded as null rather than inferred from earlier metadata.

name: BUS-CoT
full_name: A Chain-of-thought Reasoning Breast Ultrasound Dataset Covering All Histopathology Categories
paper_title: A Chain-of-thought Reasoning Breast Ultrasound Dataset Covering All Histopathology Categories
notes: BUS-CoT is an aggregate dataset constructed from peer-reviewed publications, existing public breast ultrasound datasets, and peer-reviewed online case repositories including Radiopaedia and Eurorad. It should therefore be counted as an aggregate resource rather than as a new primary acquisition family. BUS-Expert is the complete release, while BUS-Lesion is a curated subset. BUS-Lesion contains 5,163 images, including 2,694 benign and 2,469 malignant images, with 4,338 images in the released training split and 825 images in the released test split. The dataset paper reports five ultrasound device types. The Figshare resource is openly available, but the dataset-specific license was not independently verified here; the article license should not be assumed to be the dataset license.

name: DDTI
full_name: Digital Database of Thyroid Images
paper_title: An open access thyroid ultrasound image database
paper_venue: 10th International Symposium on Medical Information Processing and Analysis
notes: The original paper uses several different counting conventions: it introduces 389 study cases, while the Results section reports 347 ultrasound images from 299 patients. A widely used processed segmentation release contains 637 images. The atlas therefore records the original case count and the processed image count separately rather than treating them as equivalent. The database also contains diagnostic metadata including Bethesda/pathology information, but these are not encoded here as a standardized classification task because the exact label mapping differs across public processed releases.

name: TN-SCUI2020
full_name: Thyroid Nodule Segmentation and Classification in Ultrasound Images 2020
notes: The dataset was released for the MICCAI 2020 TN-SCUI challenge. Each image is associated with a benign/malignant label and a detailed nodule delineation. The Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3715942 identifies the accepted challenge design document rather than a peer-reviewed dataset paper or the image archive itself, so it is not entered under paper.doi or data.doi.

name: KFGNet dataset
full_name: KFGNet Thyroid Ultrasound Video Dataset
paper_title: Key-frame Guided Network for Thyroid Nodule Recognition Using Ultrasound Videos
paper_venue: Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention (MICCAI)
notes: The full dataset contains 3,668 B-mode ultrasound videos. For key-frame localization, 23,219 frames were extracted to train a Faster R-CNN-based nodule detector, and the 3,668 videos were split into 2,648 training, 504 validation, and 516 test videos. The paper reports a separate 244-video benign/malignant classification subset from the localization test cohort because the full label distribution was highly imbalanced. The repository provides the ultrasound data through Baidu Netdisk and does not state a formal dataset license. Localization is represented by the frame-level bounding-box detection annotations rather than as a separate native task.

name: TG3K
full_name: Thyroid Gland 3K
paper_title: Thyroid Region Prior Guided Attention for Ultrasound Segmentation of Thyroid Nodules
notes: TG3K is not an independent clinical acquisition. Gong et al. constructed it by extracting 2D frames from the 16 tracked 3D thyroid ultrasound records introduced by Wunderling et al. (2017), retaining frames in which the thyroid gland occupies more than 6% of the image. The 2022 paper reports 3,585 retained images. Some secondary resources report 3,583 frames; the atlas uses the count stated in the primary 2022 paper. TG3K is derived from the Thyroid Segmentation in Ultrasonography Dataset / 3DThyroid, which is cataloged as atlas entry 0109.

name: TN3K
full_name: Thyroid Nodule 3K
paper_title: Thyroid Region Prior Guided Attention for Ultrasound Segmentation of Thyroid Nodules
notes: TN3K contains 3,493 grayscale thyroid ultrasound images from 2,421 patients. Samples were selected from more than 30,000 candidate images and may contain one or multiple nodules. The public release is intended for thyroid-nodule segmentation; a benign/malignant classification label should not be assumed for TN3K merely because some project code or related repositories contain classification utilities.

name: SegThy
full_name: SegThy Dataset
paper_title: Tracked 3D Ultrasound and Deep Neural Network-Based Thyroid Segmentation Reduce Interobserver Variability in Thyroid Volumetry
notes: SegThy contains two related cohorts totaling 214 participants. Sub-dataset 1 contains 28 healthy volunteers with tracked 3D ultrasound and MRI, whereas sub-dataset 2 contains 186 clinical thyroid patients with tracked 3D ultrasound. The associated PLOS ONE volumetry study focuses on the 28-volunteer cohort.

name: Thyroid Ultrasound Cine-clip
full_name: Thyroid Ultrasound Cine-clip
paper_title: Toward Reduction in False-Positive Thyroid Nodule Biopsies with a Deep Learning-Based Risk Stratification System Using US Cine-Clip Images
data_repository: Stanford Center for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine & Imaging
notes: The dataset contains 192 biopsy-confirmed thyroid nodules from 167 patients and 17,412 cine frames. In addition to radiologist-annotated nodule segmentations, it provides demographics, lesion size and location, ACR TI-RADS descriptors, and histopathological diagnoses. The associated paper was published in Radiology: Artificial Intelligence with DOI 10.1148/ryai.210174; the separate DOI 10.71718/7m5n-rh16 identifies the dataset resource.

name: TN5000
full_name: TN5000: An Ultrasound Image Dataset for Thyroid Nodule Detection and Classification
paper_title: TN5000: An Ultrasound Image Dataset for Thyroid Nodule Detection and Classification
notes: TN5000 contains 5,000 B-mode thyroid nodule images selected from more than 30,000 candidate images. Each image contains at least one discernible nodule and is distributed with PASCAL VOC-compatible bounding-box annotations and benign/malignant labels confirmed by FNA biopsy and pathological results. The official split is 3,500 training, 500 validation, and 1,000 test images.

name: 3DThyroid
full_name: Thyroid Segmentation in Ultrasonography Dataset
paper_title: Comparison of thyroid segmentation techniques for 3D ultrasound
notes: This is the original public 3D thyroid ultrasound resource introduced by Wunderling et al. in 2017. It contains tracked 3D ultrasound records with expert thyroid-gland ground-truth segmentations. TG3K (0104) was subsequently derived from these recordings by extracting 2D frames and retaining frames in which the thyroid gland occupies more than 6% of the image area.

name: HC18
full_name: Head Circumference 2018 Challenge Dataset
paper_title: Automated measurement of fetal head circumference using 2D ultrasound images
notes: HC18 contains 1,334 fetal-head standard-plane images from 551 pregnant women. The 999-image training set includes expert-fitted ellipse outlines, pixel spacing, and head-circumference measurements in millimetres. The 335-image test set includes images and pixel spacing, while ellipse and HC ground truth are retained by the challenge organizers. The stable Zenodo concept DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.1322000; this record uses the current v2 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.1327317.

name: FETAL_PLANES_DB
full_name: FETAL_PLANES_DB: Common Maternal-Fetal Ultrasound Images
anatomy_target: Fetal abdomen | Fetal brain | Fetal femur | Fetal thorax | Maternal cervix
paper_title: Evaluation of deep convolutional neural networks for automatic classification of common maternal fetal ultrasound planes
notes: The dataset contains 12,400 routinely acquired maternal-fetal ultrasound images from 1,792 patients and 2,087 studies. Six top-level labels are provided, together with three fine-grained fetal-brain plane labels. Patient ID, ultrasound-machine ID, operator ID, and the patient-level train/test split used in the paper are included.

name: JNU-IFM
full_name: JNU-IFM Dataset for Segmenting Pubic Symphysis-Fetal Head
paper_title: The JNU-IFM dataset for segmenting pubic symphysis-fetal head
notes: JNU-IFM contains 6,224 selected frames extracted from 78 intrapartum transperineal ultrasound videos from 51 pregnant women. The released data are organized as image sequences with per-frame segmentation masks and four frame-level visibility labels. Although angle-of-progression estimation is a natural downstream use, an explicit AoP ground-truth measurement is not treated here as a native annotation task.

name: African Fetal Standard Plane Dataset
full_name: Maternal Fetal Ultrasound Planes from Low-Resource Imaging Settings in Five African Countries
anatomy_target: Fetal abdomen | Fetal brain | Fetal femur | Fetal thorax
paper_title: Generalisability of fetal ultrasound deep learning models to low-resource imaging settings in five African countries
notes: This resource contains independently acquired fetal standard-plane images from five African clinical centres and is therefore treated as a primary multi-centre acquisition. The associated study evaluates cross-country generalisation and transfer learning using FETAL_PLANES_DB (atlas ID 0202) as a high-resource source domain, but domain adaptation is not encoded as a native dataset task because the direct supervision consists of fetal-plane labels. The public Zenodo metadata currently does not expose a clear dataset-specific license, so license is left null rather than inferred from the article.

name: FPUS23
full_name: FPUS23: An Ultrasound Fetus Phantom Dataset
anatomy_target: Fetal head | Fetal abdomen | Fetal arms | Fetal legs
paper_title: FPUS23: An Ultrasound Fetus Phantom Dataset With Deep Neural Network Evaluations for Fetus Orientations, Fetal Planes, and Anatomical Features
notes: FPUS23 is a non-human fetal-phantom dataset. Diagnostic-plane labels cover 5,265 images, fetal-orientation labels cover all 15,728 images, fetal-anatomy labels cover 9,317 images, and bounding-box annotations cover 9,455 images. The GitHub repository itself carries an MIT license, while the linked source-image archive is hosted separately on Google Drive; because the image-archive license is not stated independently on the data page, access.license is left null.

name: Fetal Abdominal Structures Segmentation Dataset
full_name: Fetal Abdominal Structures Segmentation Dataset Using Ultrasonic Images
anatomy_target: Fetal abdominal aorta | Intrahepatic umbilical vein | Fetal stomach | Fetal liver
notes: The official Mendeley record describes a cohort of 169 term pregnancies and nearly 1,500 fetal abdominal-circumference images. Public reuse studies report 1,588 released images. Images were originally stored in DICOM, converted to PNG, and annotated in 3D Slicer. The dataset does not define a native classification task or a dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper.

name: ACOUSLIC-AI
full_name: Abdominal Circumference Operator-agnostic UltraSound Measurement in Low-Income Countries using Artificial Intelligence
paper_title: ACOUSLIC-AI challenge report: Fetal abdominal circumference measurement on blind-sweep ultrasound data from low-income countries
notes: The complete challenge contains 592 cases: 300 public training/development, 10 hidden validation, and 282 hidden test cases. Only the 300-case training set is distributed through Zenodo. Version 1.1 corrects circumference measurements that were too large by a factor of two in version 1.0.

name: PSFHS
full_name: PSFHS: Intrapartum Ultrasound Image Dataset for AI-based Segmentation of Pubic Symphysis and Fetal Head
paper_title: PSFHS: Intrapartum ultrasound image dataset for AI-based segmentation of pubic symphysis and fetal head
notes: PSFHS provides image/ground-truth-mask pairs only. The Scientific Data paper demonstrates that angle of progression (AoP) can be calculated from the final PS/FH segmentation masks and reports an average AoP of 98.33° ± 21.11°, but the public Zenodo archive contains the images and segmentation labels rather than a separate AoP ground-truth table. AoP measurement is therefore treated as a derived use rather than a native dataset task.

name: FOCUS
full_name: FOCUS: Four-chamber Ultrasound Image Dataset for Fetal Cardiac Biometric Measurement
notes: FOCUS was constructed from the public FETAL_PLANES_DB resource and adds fetal-heart and thoracic ellipse annotations, DOTA-format rotated boxes, segmentation masks, and biometric information. It is therefore classified as a derived dataset with parent 0202 rather than as an independent primary acquisition family. No dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper was identified.

name: Maternal-Fetal Ultrasound Video Dataset
full_name: Maternal-Fetal Ultrasound Video Dataset for End-to-end Intrapartum Biometry and Multi-task Learning
paper_title: Maternal-Fetal Ultrasouno Video Dataset for End-to-end Intrapartum Biometry and Multi-task Learning
notes: The public dataset was released on Zenodo in 2025 and subsequently described in Scientific Data in 2026. It contains 774 videos from 774 pregnant women across three institutions and devices. Landmark coordinates and derived AoP/HSD parameters are stored in landmark.json files, so biometry is treated as a native annotation task. The paper title contains the published spelling "Ultrasouno".

name: CAMUS
full_name: CAMUS
anatomy_target: Apical two-chamber view | Apical four-chamber view | Left ventricle | Left atrium
paper_title: Deep Learning for Segmentation using an Open Large-Scale Dataset in 2D Echocardiography
notes: CAMUS contains 2D echocardiographic sequences from 500 patients in apical two- and four-chamber views. Expert annotations are provided at end diastole and end systole. The structured tasks encode the native segmentation, cardiac-function measurement, and image-quality annotations rather than the broader downstream analyses that can be derived from them.

name: EchoNet-Dynamic
full_name: EchoNet-Dynamic
paper_title: Video-based AI for beat-to-beat assessment of cardiac function
notes: EchoNet-Dynamic contains 10,030 apical four-chamber echocardiography videos from 10,030 individuals. Cardiac-cycle analysis is a downstream use of the cine data, whereas the native released supervision is represented here by left-ventricular tracings and cardiac-function measurements.

name: EchoCP
full_name: EchoCP
paper_title: EchoCP: An Echocardiography Dataset in Contrast Transthoracic Echocardiography for Patent Foramen Ovale Diagnosis
notes: EchoCP contains 60 contrast transthoracic echocardiography videos from 30 patients, with two videos per patient. The released supervision supports PFO diagnosis, PFO grading, and sparse cardiac-chamber segmentation. Contrast-bubble video analysis is treated as a use of these annotations rather than as a separate native task.

name: TMED-2
full_name: Tufts Medical Echocardiogram Dataset 2
paper_title: A New Semi-Supervised Learning Benchmark for Classifying View and Diagnosing Aortic Stenosis from Echocardiograms
paper_venue: Machine Learning for Healthcare Conference (MLHC 2021), PMLR
notes: TMED-2 includes a fully labeled cohort together with additional view-only and unlabeled image sets. Semi-supervised learning is a benchmark paradigm enabled by the resource rather than a native annotation task, so it is not encoded in tasks. The two native supervised label sets are aortic-stenosis severity and cardiac-view classification.

name: EchoNet-LVH
full_name: EchoNet-LVH
anatomy_target: Left ventricle | Interventricular septum | Left-ventricular posterior wall
paper_title: High-Throughput Precision Phenotyping of Left Ventricular Hypertrophy With Cardiovascular Deep Learning
notes: EchoNet-LVH contains 12,000 labeled echocardiography videos. Left-ventricular hypertrophy phenotyping is derived from the released cardiac measurements and calculations, so the native task is represented as measurement rather than as a separate free-text regression or phenotyping task.

name: CardiacUDA / CardiacUDC
full_name: CardiacUDA / CardiacUDC
anatomy_target: Left ventricle | Right ventricle | Pulmonary artery | Cardiac chambers
paper_title: GraphEcho: Graph-Driven Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Echocardiogram Video Segmentation
notes: The associated paper describes 992 videos across two sites, while the publicly visible Kaggle package currently exposes only the A4C subset. Unsupervised domain adaptation and cross-center generalization are experimental paradigms rather than native dataset tasks; the released supervision itself is cardiac-structure segmentation.

name: EchoNet-Pediatric
full_name: EchoNet-Pediatric
paper_title: Video-Based Deep Learning for Automated Assessment of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction in Pediatric Patients
paper_venue: Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography
notes: EchoNet-Pediatric contains 7,643 labeled pediatric echocardiography videos. The released supervision consists of expert left-ventricular tracings and cardiac-function measurements. Pediatric cardiac-function assessment is therefore represented by segmentation and measurement rather than a separate free-text task.

name: CACTUS
full_name: CACTUS
paper_title: CACTUS: An Open Dataset and Framework for Automated Cardiac Assessment and Classification of Ultrasound Images Using Deep Transfer Learning
notes: CACTUS contains 37,736 cardiac-phantom ultrasound images with cardiac-view labels and image-quality grades. These are encoded as classification and quality-assessment tasks; the phantom origin is retained explicitly under anatomy.

name: MIMIC-IV-Echo
full_name: MIMIC-IV-Echo
anatomy_target: Cardiac chambers | Systolic function | Diastolic function | Cardiac valves | Aorta and great vessels | Doppler hemodynamics
modality_type: B-mode | M-mode | Color Doppler | Spectral Doppler
paper_title: MIMIC-IV-Echo: Echocardiogram Matched Subset
notes: MIMIC-IV-Echo v1.0.1 contains 206,488 echocardiography studies from 91,372 patients. The DICOM subset contains 524,137 files from 7,228 transthoracic echocardiography studies and 4,572 patients. The resource links echocardiographic imaging and structured measurements to MIMIC-IV. Representation learning, view analysis, and multimodal clinical research are important downstream uses, but the native structured supervision recorded here is measurement metadata.

name: POCUS Dataset for COVID-19 Detection
full_name: A Lung Ultrasound Dataset for COVID-19 Detection
license: Mixed per-source licenses, including CC BY 4.0, CC BY-NC 4.0, and source-specific terms
paper_title: Accelerating Detection of Lung Pathologies with Explainable Ultrasound Image Analysis
notes: The stable paper release contains 261 recordings from 216 patients: 202 videos and 59 static images. It contains 92 COVID-19, 73 bacterial-pneumonia, 90 healthy, and 6 non-COVID viral-pneumonia recordings assembled from 41 sources. The continuously updated metadata currently lists more source records than the stable paper release, so the structured scale above follows the stable 261-record release. Disease labels and visible lung-ultrasound patterns were reviewed by medical experts. Four-level severity scores were later added for 136 videos. The optional uninformative class is an auxiliary out-of-distribution resource rather than a core diagnostic class. Patient- or video-level splitting is required to prevent frame-level data leakage.

name: COVIDx-US
full_name: COVIDx-US Open-Access Lung Ultrasound Benchmark Dataset
license: GNU AGPL 3.0 for repository materials; source media retain source-specific terms
paper_title: COVIDx-US: An Open-Access Benchmark Dataset of Ultrasound Imaging Data for AI-Driven COVID-19 Analytics
notes: The repository reports 242 videos and 29,651 processed frames. The published paper describes a different version snapshot with 173 videos and 21,570 frames from 147 patients, while repository history associates the larger 242-video collection with an earlier benchmark version and later adds LUSS metadata. Repository masks remove embedded text and symbols and are not anatomical segmentation labels, so segmentation is not encoded as a native task. The repository does not host the original videos; scripts retrieve media from multiple external public sources.

name: LUSS_phantom
full_name: Lung Ultrasound COVID Phantom Dataset Used for Training a Machine Learning Model
anatomy_target: Ribs | Pleural line | A-lines | B-lines | B-line confluence
paper_title: Deep learning for real-time multi-class segmentation of artefacts in lung ultrasound
data_repository: University of Leeds Research Data Repository
notes: The dataset contains 564 manually annotated frames generated from two-second cine loops acquired from a COVID-19 lung-ultrasound training phantom using multiple diagnostic ultrasound systems. Five annotators labelled 100 images each and a senior sonographer labelled another 64 images. B-line artefact quantification is a downstream use derived from the segmentation masks rather than a separate native annotation task. No patient data are included. The separate clinical transfer-learning dataset described in the paper is available only upon request and is outside this public resource.

name: Lung Ultrasound Images for Automated AI-based Lung Disease Classification
full_name: A Dataset of Lung Ultrasound Images for Automated AI-based Lung Disease Classification
paper_title: A dataset of lung ultrasound images for automated AI-based lung disease classification
notes: The dataset contains 1,062 images from 149 Ugandan patients: 338 images from 27 patients classified as probably COVID-19, 362 images from 67 patients with other lung disease, and 362 images from 55 healthy-lung patients. The patient-level split contains 723 training, 198 validation, and 141 test images. Mendeley version 2 adds the original unprocessed data together with processing, cleaning, and sorting scripts.

name: POCUS LUS Datasets
full_name: POCUS Lung Ultrasound Datasets
license: CC BY 4.0 on Figshare; upstream source-specific rights vary
notes: This resource contains only 10 static images: six COVID-19, three bacterial-pneumonia, and one normal image, associated with eight distinct patient/source IDs. File-level verification showed that all 10 images are byte-identical to same-named files in atlas dataset 0401. It is therefore recorded as an exact subset of 0401 rather than as an independent derivative. The Figshare record itself contains no provenance statement, label table, patient metadata, selection criteria, bounding boxes, or segmentation masks.

name: PU2756
full_name: A Pulmonary Ultrasound Dataset for Tumor Segmentation and Classification
paper_title: A Pulmonary Ultrasound Dataset for Tumor Segmentation and Classification
notes: PU2756 contains 2,756 B-mode pulmonary-ultrasound images from 2,756 unique patients, with one image per patient: 1,755 malignant and 1,001 benign. Expert annotations include pixel-level pulmonary-tumor masks, while benign/malignant labels are confirmed through biopsy pathology. The public Figshare v1 record provides images.zip, masks.zip, and five_fold_split.xlsx. The five-fold partition is retained in the release metadata but is not encoded as a single train/validation/test split in this atlas entry.

name: Fatty Liver Ultrasound
full_name: Dataset of B-mode Fatty Liver Ultrasound Images
paper_title: Transfer learning with deep convolutional neural network for liver steatosis assessment in ultrasound images
paper_venue: International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
notes: The dataset contains ten consecutive 434 x 636 B-mode frames from each of 55 severely obese patients. Wedge-biopsy steatosis percentage is provided as the reference standard. Because the continuous biopsy percentage is available, the former free-text "Regression" task is represented as a native measurement task rather than as a separate research paradigm.

name: B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver
full_name: Ultrasound Data of a Variety of Liver Masses
notes: The complete Version 2 contains 120 studies, 120 series, and 1,859 DICOM instances totaling 272.16 GB. Clinical diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up data are provided. Lesion characterization reference standards include pathology and contrast-enhanced cross-sectional imaging. Treatment-response reference standards are available for many HCC cases, but no single standardized treatment-response label schema is documented here, so treatment-response assessment and temporal analysis are treated as downstream uses rather than separate native tasks. No consistent bounding-box or pixel-wise lesion annotations are released.

name: Annotated Ultrasound Liver Images
full_name: Annotated Ultrasound Liver Images
anatomy_target: Liver | Liver mass | Ultrasound scan region
paper_title: Improving artificial intelligence pipeline for liver malignancy diagnosis using ultrasound images and video frames
notes: The public release contains exactly 735 JPG images: 435 malignant, 200 benign, and 100 normal. It is an annotated public subset associated with a larger study of 50,063 images and video frames from 11,468 patients; the full study cohorts are not publicly included here. Detection is a possible downstream use of the polygon annotations, but no independent bounding-box annotation is released, so detection is not encoded as a native task.

name: GBCU
full_name: Gallbladder Cancer Ultrasound Dataset
anatomy_target: Gallbladder | Gallbladder pathology | Adjacent liver region
paper_title: Surpassing the Human Accuracy: Detecting Gallbladder Cancer From USG Images With Curriculum Learning
notes: GBCU contains 1,255 B-mode gallbladder ultrasound images from 218 patients. No pixel-wise segmentation masks are provided; the spatial supervision consists of expert bounding boxes. Access is application-based under the custom GBCU license agreement.

name: GBUSV
full_name: Gallbladder Ultrasound Video Dataset
paper_title: Unsupervised Contrastive Learning of Image Representations from Ultrasound Videos with Hard Negative Mining
notes: The original release contains 64 videos and 15,800 frames. Videos contain 43-888 frames and were resized to 360 x 480 pixels. The current application agreement is labeled GBUSV v2.0, whereas the project page still documents the original 64-video release. Self-supervised representation learning is the research paradigm used in the associated paper rather than a native dataset task, so only video-level classification is encoded under tasks.

name: liver_ultrasound
full_name: liver_ultrasound Computer Vision Project
notes: Version v11 contains 400 images with a 220/120/60 train/validation/test split. Patient count, acquisition source, annotator details, diagnostic reference standards, and the semantics of several abbreviated detection classes are not documented. Verification is therefore marked partial even though the public project structure and counts are available.

name: BEHSOF
full_name: BEHSOF - Advanced Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Dataset with Clinical Metadata and Ultrasound Images for Deep Learning Models
notes: BEHSOF contains 113 participants: 18 from Taleghani Hospital and 95 from Behbood Clinic. Clinical data include demographics, anthropometric measurements, blood tests, CAP score, elasticity/E score, and FibroScan results. The original free-text tasks "Regression" and "Multimodal Prediction" are downstream modeling formulations; the native structured supervision is represented here as grading and measurement metadata.

name: Saudi NAFLD Liver Ultrasound Dataset
full_name: Large Annotated Ultrasound Dataset of Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver from Saudi Hospitals for Analysis and Applications
paper_title: Large annotated ultrasound dataset of non-alcoholic fatty liver from Saudi hospitals for analysis and applications
notes: The dataset contains 10,352 standardized 768 x 1024 PNG images from 384 patients: 8,772 grayscale and 1,580 color images. Full-image labels are based on corresponding liver-biopsy results. No bounding boxes, segmentation masks, patient IDs, examination dates, raw NAS scores, or biopsy reports are released. The OSF files were not directly accessible during verification, so verification remains partial.

name: SMC-LUD
full_name: Samsung Medical Center Liver Ultrasound Dataset
license: CC BY 4.0 with repository and paper restrictions limiting use to non-commercial research
paper_title: SMC-LUD: Large-Scale B-Mode Liver Ultrasound Dataset for Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Hemangioma Classification
notes: SMC-LUD contains 5,385 anonymized images from 1,021 patients: 2,716 HCC images from 600 patients and 2,669 hemangioma images from 421 patients. HCC metadata include tumor size and UICC/AJCC pT stages. Clean and Caliper image subsets are provided; no segmentation masks are reported. Figshare displays CC BY 4.0, while the repository and paper additionally impose a non-commercial research-only restriction, which is recorded explicitly under access.

name: LUMINOUS
full_name: LUMINOUS Database: Lumbar Multifidus Muscle Segmentation from Ultrasound Images
anatomy_target: Lumbar multifidus muscle | Left lumbar multifidus at L5 | Right lumbar multifidus at L5
paper_title: LUMINOUS Database: Lumbar Multifidus Muscle Segmentation from Ultrasound Images
notes: LUMINOUS contains 109 subject datasets with left- and right-sided lumbar multifidus ultrasound images acquired at L5 in prone and standing positions. Cross-sectional area and echo-intensity quantification can be derived from the images and masks, but the native released supervision is muscle segmentation, so those analyses are not encoded as separate tasks.

name: deepMTJ test set
full_name: deepMTJ Test Set
anatomy_target: Lateral gastrocnemius muscle-tendon junction | Medial gastrocnemius muscle-tendon junction
paper_title: A Human-Centered Machine-Learning Approach for Muscle-Tendon Junction Tracking in Ultrasound Images
notes: The public deepMTJ test set contains 1,344 B-mode ultrasound images acquired with three ultrasound systems. Ground truth is defined from four specialist annotations. The associated study evaluates MTJ tracking and cross-device generalization, but the released annotation itself is per-image MTJ localization; tracking and benchmark generalization are therefore not encoded as separate native tasks.

name: FALLMUD
full_name: FALLMUD
paper_title: AW-Net: Automatic Muscle Structure Analysis on B-Mode Ultrasound Images for Injury Prevention
notes: FALLMUD contains 812 B-mode ultrasound images and combines two earlier image sets with complementary fascicle and aponeurosis masks. It is therefore recorded as an aggregate resource rather than a new independent acquisition. Muscle-architecture quantification is a downstream use derived from these segmentation masks and is not encoded as a separate native task.

name: TUS-REC2024
full_name: TUS-REC2024: Trackerless Ultrasound Reconstruction Challenge 2024
paper_title: TUS-REC2024: A Challenge to Reconstruct 3D Freehand Ultrasound Without External Tracker
notes: TUS-REC2024 contains 2,040 freehand forearm ultrasound scans from 85 healthy volunteers. The native supervision consists of synchronized per-frame 4x4 spatial transformations. These support relative-pose estimation, spatial registration, and trackerless 3D reconstruction, which are retained as the three native technical tasks.

name: Machine Learning-Driven Heckmatt Grading in FSHD
full_name: Machine Learning-Driven Heckmatt Grading in FSHD
paper_title: Machine learning-driven Heckmatt grading in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy: A novel pathway for musculoskeletal ultrasound analysis
notes: The dataset contains 25,005 B-mode ultrasound images from 290 participants, including 180 healthy participants and 110 participants with FSHD. Healthy-versus-FSHD analysis is represented by the participant-level classification labels, while Heckmatt grading and muscle segmentation are encoded separately according to their native annotations.

name: Transverse Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Dataset for NMD Assessment
full_name: Transverse Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Dataset for Neuromuscular Disease Assessment
anatomy_target: Biceps brachii | Tibialis anterior | Medial gastrocnemius
paper_title: Deep Learning Segmentation of Transverse Musculoskeletal Ultrasound Images for Neuromuscular Disease Assessment
notes: The dataset contains 3,917 transverse musculoskeletal ultrasound images from 1,283 subjects. Expert cross-sectional-area masks are the principal spatial annotations. Healthy/abnormal status and grayscale-derived quantitative information are retained as classification and measurement annotations rather than as free-text downstream assessment tasks.

name: Robotic and Handheld Lumbar Spine Ultrasound
full_name: A Large, Paired Dataset of Robotic and Handheld Lumbar Spine Ultrasound with Ground-truth CT Benchmarking
paper_title: A large, paired dataset of robotic and handheld lumbar spine ultrasound with ground-truth CT benchmarking
notes: The resource includes 223 handheld and 375 robot-assisted lumbar-spine ultrasound scans. The 6,091 expert-annotated frames comprise 2,353 handheld and 3,738 robot-assisted frames selected from nine volunteers. Paired CT scans, synchronized ultrasound tracking data, and CT-derived 3D vertebral surface models support registration and reconstruction. The former empty classification block has been removed because no native classification labels are described.

name: AI/ML-ready Knee Ultrasound Dataset
full_name: Development of an AI/ML-ready Knee Ultrasound Dataset in a Population-based Cohort
aliases: Knee Ultrasound Dataset in a Population-based Cohort | JoCoHS Knee Ultrasound Dataset
paper_title: Associations and Diagnostic Accuracy of Ultrasound Features in Knee Osteoarthritis: Cross-Sectional Results From a Large Community-Based Cohort
notes: This dataset is not currently represented elsewhere in the atlas and is suitable for inclusion as a primary musculoskeletal ultrasound resource. It originates from the population-based Johnston County Health Study (JoCoHS) and was created as an AI/ML-ready FAIR resource for research on knee osteoarthritis and related ultrasound phenotypes. Associated publications describe a standardized protocol with seven images per knee. Expert readers scored osteoarthritis-related ultrasound features including effusion/synovitis, Power Doppler signal, osteophytes, cartilage damage, meniscal extrusion, popliteal cysts, and calcium crystal deposition, with disagreements adjudicated by a third reader. However, the publications specifically state that the Harvard Dataverse currently provides all ultrasound images and limited metadata. Because public availability of the final expert feature scores could not be independently confirmed from the currently accessible Dataverse metadata, those scores are not encoded as native public annotations in this atlas entry. The associated 2025 cohort analysis included 861 participants and 1,711 knees with complete imaging data from a 902-participant Johnston County Health Study cohort. These study-cohort counts are not used as the public dataset scale because the Harvard Dataverse is a versioned resource and the publicly summarized resource size is 7,571 ultrasound images. The currently accessible indexed Harvard Dataverse information identifies version 5.1. A dataset-specific reusable license could not be independently confirmed, so access.license is left null. Verification is marked partial because the Dataverse landing page could not be fully inspected from the verification environment.

name: UK Biobank carotid ultrasound
full_name: UK Biobank Carotid Ultrasound Imaging Resource
notes: This entry represents the UK Biobank carotid-ultrasound resource family rather than a single frozen benchmark release. Participant and image counts therefore vary by selected data field and release. The resource supports carotid phenotype and intima-media-thickness analysis through linkage with UK Biobank participant metadata. It is application-controlled rather than an open-download dataset.

name: CUBS
full_name: Carotid Ultrasound Boundary Study
anatomy_target: Common carotid artery | Lumen-intima boundary | Media-adventitia boundary
paper_title: Carotid Ultrasound Boundary Study (CUBS): An Open Multicenter Analysis of Computerized Intima-Media Thickness Measurement Systems and Their Clinical Impact
notes: CUBS contains 2,176 common-carotid-artery B-mode images from 1,088 participants. Its core spatial annotations are paired lumen-intima and media-adventitia boundaries rather than ordinary filled binary masks, so they are represented as surface/boundary segmentation. Carotid intima-media thickness is a native quantitative use of these paired boundaries.

name: CCA
full_name: CCA Carotid Artery Ultrasound Segmentation Dataset Used by MI-SegNet
anatomy_target: Carotid artery lumen | Carotid artery region
paper_title: MI-SegNet: Mutual Information-Based US Segmentation for Unseen Domain Generalization
notes: CCA contains 2,307 B-mode carotid-ultrasound images: 2,107 training images and 200 held-out validation images. Domain generalization across ultrasound devices is the experimental setting of the MI-SegNet study rather than a native dataset task, so only segmentation is encoded under tasks. No standalone data DOI or explicit dataset license was confirmed.

name: CCAUI
full_name: Common Carotid Artery Ultrasound Images
aliases: Common Carotid Artery Ultrasound Images Dataset
notes: The public release contains 1,100 carotid ultrasound images from 11 participants and 1,100 corresponding expert-verified masks, for 2,200 PNG files in total. Each participant contributes 100 images and was examined on the left and right sides at least once. The resource can support carotid geometry measurement, but no independent measurement ground-truth table is distributed; measurement is therefore treated as a mask-derived use rather than a native dataset task. No dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper was identified.

name: BITE
full_name: Brain Images of Tumors for Evaluation
paper_title: Online database of clinical MR and ultrasound images of brain tumors
notes: BITE contains data from 14 brain-tumor patients organized into four downloadable groups: pre-/post-resection ultrasound, preoperative MRI with pre-resection ultrasound, pre-/post-operative MRI, and preoperative MRI with post-resection ultrasound. Ultrasound data include original 2D B-mode sweeps and reconstructed 3D volumes. Tumor segmentation masks are not provided. Images primarily use MINC format. Target-registration-error analysis is an evaluation derived from the landmark annotations rather than a separate native task.

name: RESECT
full_name: REtroSpective Evaluation of Cerebral Tumors
paper_title: REtroSpective Evaluation of Cerebral Tumors (RESECT): A clinical database of pre-operative MRI and intra-operative ultrasound in low-grade glioma surgeries
notes: RESECT contains 23 low-grade-glioma surgery cases with preoperative MRI and intraoperative ultrasound. The core resource provides anatomical landmarks for MRI-iUS registration evaluation. Related extension resources add tumor and resection-cavity segmentation labels, but those extensions are not treated here as native annotations of the core RESECT entry. No explicit reusable data license was confirmed on the accessible landing page.

name: Dataset of 3D ultrasound neuroimages
full_name: Dataset of 3D Ultrasound Neuroimages and Supporting Info
notes: This is a small unlabeled 3D transfontanellar ultrasound neuroimage resource with supporting files. The earlier atlas entry listed data augmentation, 2D slice synthesis, GAN training, and representation research as tasks, but these are modeling uses rather than native annotations. Because the current schema requires at least one task for an unlabeled reusable image resource, it is categorized under the generic pretraining task. No consistent manual semantic-segmentation labels or dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper were verified. The entry was updated from the earlier 2025 Zenodo record 14917169 to the 2026 record with supporting information.

name: ReMIND
full_name: The Brain Resection Multimodal Imaging Database
anatomy_target: Brain tumor | Brain parenchyma | Resection cavity | Residual tumor tissue | Resected tissue
paper_title: ReMIND: The Brain Resection Multimodal Imaging Database
notes: ReMIND contains 114 neurosurgical cases with preoperative MRI, intraoperative MRI, and intraoperative ultrasound. Expert segmentations include tumor, brain parenchyma, resection cavity, and residual/resected tissue labels. Image-guided neurosurgery is the broader clinical application of the resource; the native structured tasks are represented here as segmentation and registration.

name: BraTioUS
full_name: BraTioUS - Brain Tumor Intraoperative Ultrasound Dataset
notes: BraTioUS contains 1,669 intraoperative B-mode ultrasound images from 142 glioma patients, together with tumor segmentation masks and a metadata spreadsheet. Tumor/no-tumor image classification can be derived from the segmentation masks, but no independent native classification annotation is required, so classification is not encoded as a separate task. This entry uses the latest verified Zenodo record dated 2026-06-22; the concept DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.16887362.

name: The Open Kidney Ultrasound Data Set
full_name: The Open Kidney Ultrasound Data Set
anatomy_target: Native kidney | Transplanted kidney | Renal capsule | Renal cortex | Renal medulla | Central echogenic complex
paper_title: The Open Kidney Ultrasound Data Set
paper_venue: International Workshop on Advances in Simplifying Medical Ultrasound
notes: The dataset contains 514 unique anonymized B-mode kidney ultrasound images from 514 distinct patients, including native and transplanted kidneys. Twenty additional duplicate copies are included for annotation-consistency assessment, producing 534 delivered image files in total. In addition to kidney-type and view-type labels, the resource includes image-quality labels and fine-grained expert polygon annotations for the renal capsule, cortex, medulla, and central echogenic complex. The GitHub repository provides code and annotation resources, while source ultrasound images require registration and manual approval before release through UBC OneDrive.

name: Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy
full_name: Prostate MRI and Ultrasound With Pathology and Coordinates of Tracked Biopsy
anatomy_target: Prostate gland | Prostate cancer-suspicious region | Prostate biopsy core
paper_title: Targeted biopsy in the detection of prostate cancer using an office based magnetic resonance ultrasound fusion device
notes: This is an independent multimodal prostate imaging collection derived from tracked MRI-ultrasound fusion biopsy sessions. The current TCIA version contains 1,151 participants, 2,799 studies, 4,819 series, and 102,397 MR/US DICOM images. Ultrasound is 3D transrectal imaging. The collection also provides target and biopsy spreadsheets, STL prostate/ROI surfaces, biopsy overlay files, and a related DICOM-annotation resource. That external annotation resource is described here rather than placed in family.related because it does not have a four-digit atlas ID.

name: μ-RegPro
full_name: MR to Ultrasound Registration for Prostate Challenge
anatomy_target: Prostate gland | Prostate anatomical landmarks | Prostate lesions
notes: μ-RegPro is an independent UCLH prostate MRI-TRUS registration dataset derived from participants in the SmartTarget Biopsy Clinical Trial and is unrelated to the UCLA/TCIA Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy acquisition family (1001). Of 141 enrolled men, 108 had transverse ultrasound acquisitions suitable for the challenge and were included. The 108 cases were split into 65 training, 8 validation, and 35 test cases. The challenge homepage is https://muregpro.github.io/. The challenge-description resource has DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7844907, and the separately released 2026 holdout-test resource has DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19414480. These are retained in notes rather than under data.additional_resources because v3 data metadata intentionally supports only repository, url, doi, and version.

name: Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation Dataset
full_name: Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation Dataset
paper_title: MicroSegNet: A deep learning approach for prostate segmentation on micro-ultrasound images
notes: This is an independent University of Florida micro-ultrasound acquisition family and is unrelated to the UCLA/TCIA Prostate-MRI-US-Biopsy dataset (1001) or the UCLH μ-RegPro MRI-TRUS registration dataset (1002). The associated MicroSegNet paper trains on 55 patients and evaluates on 20 held-out patients. Later studies commonly process the 3D scans as axial slices, but the atlas records the native public resource at the patient/volume level rather than treating derived slice counts as the primary dataset scale.

name: Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation
full_name: Kaggle Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation Dataset
aliases: US Nerve Segmentation | Nerve Segment Dataset
notes: The Kaggle competition ran from May 19 to August 18, 2016. Images are 2D grayscale ultrasound frames of the neck used to identify the brachial plexus for regional-anesthesia applications. The training set contains 5,635 images from 47 subjects and corresponding binary masks; the test set contains 5,508 unlabeled images from non-overlapping subjects. Kaggle notes that the dataset can contain identical or highly similar frames and that human annotations may include noise or mistakes. No dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper or dataset DOI was identified. The competition page labels the license as "Subject to Competition Rules", so access.license is left null and the rule-acceptance requirement is represented under access.requirements.

name: UBPD
full_name: Ultrasonic Brachial Plexus Dataset
paper_title: MallesNet: A multi-object assistance based network for brachial plexus segmentation in ultrasound images
notes: UBPD was constructed from 101 patients for multi-structure segmentation in brachial plexus ultrasound. Professional anesthesiologists acquired the ultrasound data and manually annotated the brachial plexus nerve, muscle, vein, and artery using LabelMe. The paper contains an internal inconsistency in dataset size: the abstract, highlights, and contribution summary state 1,055 images, whereas Section 3 states 1,052 images and the reported experimental split contains 955 training plus 97 test images, also totaling 1,052. Therefore, 1,052 is used as the canonical image count. The original author-hosted dataset website was unreachable during verification on 2026-09-04. A current secondary ultrasound-dataset catalog describes the resource as requiring citation and contact with administrators for specific research-use terms; because the original access terms and files could not be independently inspected, the license is left null and verification.status is set to partial.

name: Regional-US Brachial Plexus
full_name: Brachial Plexus and Needle Annotations Data in Ultrasound Videos
aliases: Regional-US Brachial Plexus Dataset | Brachial Plexus and Needle Annotations
paper_title: Nerve Block Target Localization and Needle Guidance for Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound Guided Regional Anesthesia
paper_venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
notes: This is a multi-device brachial-plexus ultrasound video dataset designed for ultrasound-guided regional-anesthesia research. The public repository was created and the first data were uploaded in December 2022; needle annotation data were added subsequently. The repository contains scanner-specific data from Esaote MyLab One, Sonosite M-Turbo, and Butterfly iQ systems, together with brachial-plexus annotations, active-contour-assisted masks, and a Sonosite needle-annotation subset. Although bounding-box annotation text files are present, the repository explicitly states that individual boxes have no independent meaning and that their union is used to define the nerve-plexus mask; therefore, object detection is not listed as a native dataset task. The authors report 227 subjects, 227 videos, and approximately 41,000 annotated frames. Detailed device-specific counts account for 226 videos and 40,200 frames, while the repository additionally contains one annotated demo video; the exact correspondence of this demo video to the reported total is not explicitly documented. The repository does not provide a machine-readable open-source/data license, but states that the deidentified videos are shared under a non-commercial data use agreement.

name: Ovarian Ultrasound Image Dataset
full_name: Ovarian Ultrasound Image Dataset
notes: This Kaggle release contains 6,879 grayscale ovarian ultrasound images for five-class ovarian-condition classification: healthy ovary, dominant follicle, polycystic ovary, simple cyst, and complex cyst. The class counts reported on the data card sum exactly to 6,879 images. No segmentation, detection, landmark, or measurement annotations are documented, so classification is treated as the only native task. Dataset provenance is incompletely documented. The Kaggle page does not report the number of patients, acquisition institution or country, scanner, transducer, acquisition period, official train/validation/test split, or a dedicated dataset publication. The uploader account is named "UCI Machine Learning", but its Kaggle profile identifies it as Universal Computing Innovations; therefore, this dataset should not be described as an official UCI Machine Learning Repository resource. The Kaggle data card lists the dataset license as CC0: Public Domain. Verification is consequently marked partial despite the dataset being publicly downloadable.

name: PCOS Dataset
full_name: Figshare Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Ultrasound Dataset
aliases: Figshare PCOS Dataset | PCOS Ultrasound Dataset
notes: This resource was posted to Figshare on 2024-11-12 by Indirani A and is intended for automated PCOS detection and explainable-AI research. The Figshare metadata explicitly states that the images were sourced from publicly available datasets, so this entry is classified as an aggregate rather than a primary clinical dataset. The primary Figshare record reports 12,680 ultrasound images but does not document the contributing source datasets, patient count, acquisition institutions, scanner information, official train/validation/test split, or class distribution. Later publications using the same Figshare DOI generally describe the data as grayscale ovarian ultrasound images for binary PCOS classification and commonly report 11,784 usable images, comprising 6,784 PCOS and 5,000 non-PCOS images. This discrepancy cannot be fully reconciled from the public metadata, so 12,680 is retained as the canonical repository count and verification.status is set to partial. No dedicated associated dataset publication is listed by Figshare or the NLM Dataset Catalog. Later papers using the resource are therefore treated as downstream studies rather than as the dataset's primary paper.

name: MMOTU
full_name: Multi-Modality Ovarian Tumor Ultrasound Image Dataset
aliases: Multi-Modality Ovarian Tumor Ultrasound | OTU_2D + OTU_CEUS
paper_title: Unsupervised cross-domain semantic segmentation on multi-modality ovarian tumor ultrasound data
data_repository: Google Drive via official GitHub repository
notes: MMOTU is a single-center multi-modality ovarian tumor ultrasound dataset collected at Beijing Shijitan Hospital, Capital Medical University. It contains 1,639 images from 294 patients and consists of the OTU_2D and OTU_CEUS subsets. The GitHub repository was created in July 2022 and the original arXiv description was released in 2022, so 2022 is used as the dataset release year. The work was subsequently published in Pattern Recognition under the revised title "Unsupervised cross-domain semantic segmentation on multi-modality ovarian tumor ultrasound data." Pixel-wise semantic annotations and global tumor-category annotations were produced by 27 Obstetrics and Gynecology experts. Each image was annotated by one expert and checked by another, with pathological reports used as reference. The official MMOTU segmentation code uses two classes, "background" and "OvarianTumor", and binary mask files with the suffix "_binary.PNG". Although unsupervised domain adaptation is the principal methodological setting investigated in the associated paper, it is not listed as a native dataset task because it is an experimental learning setting rather than an additional annotation type. The GitHub repository contains an Apache-2.0 LICENSE inherited from MMSegmentation and explicitly copyrighted to the MMSegmentation authors. No separate dataset-specific license was identified for the MMOTU image files, so access.license is conservatively left null.

name: PCOSGen
full_name: PCOSGen Dataset for Automatic Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Classification
paper_title: Auto-PCOS Classification Challenge
notes: PCOSGen was developed for the Auto-PCOS Classification Challenge and aggregates ovarian ultrasound frames collected from multiple internet resources, including YouTube, ultrasoundcases.info, and Kaggle. The dataset therefore does not represent a single prospective or retrospective clinical cohort and is classified as an aggregate dataset. The original PCOSGen-train release appeared on Zenodo in December 2023 under record 10430727. The authors subsequently released an updated training dataset under record 14592001 on January 3, 2025 and explicitly requested that researchers use the updated release rather than previous versions. It contains 3,200 images, with inconsistent resolutions but most images approximately 300 x 300 pixels. PCOSGen-test contains 1,468 images. Test labels were initially withheld during the Auto-PCOS challenge and were later made public. The updated test release is Zenodo record 14591782. Together, the official training and test resources contain 4,668 ultrasound images. The latest Zenodo descriptions provide two levels of classification: a general normal-versus-abnormal label and, for abnormal images, a specific indication of whether a polycystic ovary is visible. No native segmentation, detection, landmark, or measurement annotations are documented. A dataset-specific license could not be unambiguously confirmed from the currently retrievable Zenodo metadata, so access.license is conservatively left null.

name: OPULM PALA
full_name: Open Platform for Ultrasound Localization Microscopy - Performance Assessment of Localization Algorithms
paper_title: Performance benchmarking of microbubble-localization algorithms for ultrasound localization microscopy
notes: OPULM PALA contains six benchmark datasets for ultrasound localization microscopy, including simulated and in vivo acquisitions. The resource is designed to assess microbubble localization, trajectory recovery, and vascular reconstruction. Algorithm benchmarking is the evaluation purpose rather than an additional native dataset task. Atlas entry 1302 is related through the same ULM benchmarking work but represents a distinct rat-brain acquisition and public data release, so neither resource is treated as the parent of the other.

name: In vivo rat brain for Ultrasound Localization Microscopy
full_name: In vivo Rat Brain for Ultrasound Localization Microscopy: Raw and Beamformed Data
paper_title: Performance benchmarking of microbubble-localization algorithms for ultrasound localization microscopy
notes: This resource contains in vivo rat-brain ultrasound-localization-microscopy acquisitions released as raw RF data and beamformed ultrasound data, together with acquisition metadata. It does not provide a unified semantic disease or anatomical label set. Microbubble localization and tracking are important downstream ULM processing steps, but the reusable native resource is primarily suited to beamforming, reconstruction, and signal-analysis research. It shares the associated benchmarking paper with atlas entry 1301 but is a distinct acquisition and release rather than a subset or derived version of 1301.

name: Mouse Brain Tumor Ultrasound
full_name: High-Resolution Ultrasound Data for AI-Based Segmentation in Mouse Brain Tumor
paper_title: High-Resolution Ultrasound Data for AI-Based Segmentation in Mouse Brain Tumor
notes: The dataset contains 1,856 high-resolution mouse-brain ultrasound images, including 1,448 tumor images and 408 no-tumor images. Its native supervision is pixel-wise brain-tumor segmentation. Binary tumor/no-tumor classification is directly derivable from the segmentation annotations and is therefore not duplicated as a separate native task.

name: Open-3DULM / Transcranial mice brain
full_name: 3D Transcranial Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Awake Mice
paper_title: 3D Transcranial Ultrasound Localization Microscopy in Awake Mice: Protocol and Open-Source Pipeline
notes: Open-3DULM contains spatiotemporal transcranial ultrasound-localization- microscopy acquisitions from five awake mice and an open processing pipeline. The resource is intended for 3D/4D ULM reconstruction, microvascular analysis, and cerebral blood-flow research. Because no unified semantic or quantitative ground-truth annotation set is documented in the atlas source, microvascular analysis and blood-flow quantification are treated as downstream analyses; the native technical tasks are represented as reconstruction and signal analysis.

name: Spinal Cord Injury Ultrasound Dataset
full_name: Open-source Ultrasound Dataset for Spinal Cord Injury Localization and Anatomical Segmentation
paper_title: A novel open-source ultrasound dataset with deep learning benchmarks for spinal cord injury localization and anatomical segmentation
notes: The dataset contains 10,223 sagittal B-mode porcine spinal-cord ultrasound images, comprising 4,467 pre-injury and 5,756 post-injury images. It provides injury-status labels, anatomical segmentation masks, and injury-localization bounding boxes for 2,245 images. Because the spatial injury annotations are bounding boxes, the native spatial task is encoded as detection rather than duplicated as both localization and detection. A specific reusable dataset license was not confirmed.

name: ULMShare
full_name: ULMShare Ultrasound Localization Microscopy Data Resource
notes: ULMShare contains 99 ultrasound-localization-microscopy acquisitions from 61 mice and is approximately 30 TB in size. It provides raw channel data, acquisition metadata, and selected ULM reconstructions and microbubble trajectories. Vascular imaging and algorithm benchmarking are downstream research uses rather than separate native tasks. No dedicated peer-reviewed dataset paper or explicit reusable dataset license was verified.

name: Clinical Ultrasound Image Repository
full_name: Clinical Ultrasound Image Repository
anatomy_target: Abdomen | Heart | Obstetric and gynecologic anatomy
notes: The repository contains 2,000 clinical ultrasound studies from 2,000 subjects, with approximately one third of the resource assigned to abdominal, cardiac, and obstetric/gynecologic imaging. The data are distributed as clinical DICOM resources with metadata but without a unified manual semantic-label set. Metadata-based anatomy or view studies are possible downstream uses, but no consistent atlas-wide anatomy/view ground truth is encoded as a native task. Because the resource is primarily useful as a broad unlabeled multi-anatomy imaging collection, it is categorized under pretraining. Anonymous S3 access is available, and the resource is managed by the MONAI Development Team.

name: USenhance 2023
full_name: Ultrasound Image Enhancement Challenge 2023
anatomy_target: Thyroid | Carotid artery | Liver | Kidney | Breast
notes: The challenge design proposed 1,500 low/high-quality pairs from 109 patients, with 1,050 training pairs and 450 test pairs. The current public downloads expose the full 1,050 training pairs but only 364 low-quality test inputs, with no public test reference images. The missing 86 proposed test cases correspond to the breast range under the released ID scheme. Public training pairs comprise 202 breast, 286 carotid-artery, 122 kidney, 149 liver, and 291 thyroid pairs. The challenge-design DOI 10.5281/zenodo.7841250 is retained as a verification source rather than encoded as a dataset paper. The proposal states CC BY-SA for data use without specifying a version; its own document record is licensed CC BY-ND 4.0, which applies to the proposal rather than the ultrasound image archive.

name: Chinese multi-organ ultrasound image-text datasets
full_name: Chinese Breast, Thyroid, and Liver Ultrasound Image-Text Datasets Used for Ultrasound Report Generation
paper_title: Ultrasound Report Generation With Cross-Modality Feature Alignment via Unsupervised Guidance
data_repository: Google Drive via author GitHub repository
notes: The paper reports 7,390 patients rather than 7,390 image-report pairs and does not separately state a report count. The current public archive contains 7,364 JSON records and 17,149 images. Every released record has a non-empty finding field and two image-path entries, although 21 records repeat the same image path rather than naming two distinct images. The manifests reference 14,707 distinct image files, leaving 2,442 released images unreferenced. The public record count is 26 lower than the paper cohort count across the three organs. No dataset-specific license was identified. Unsupervised report clustering, pseudo-label learning, and image-text feature alignment are methodological settings of the associated study rather than additional native annotation tasks.

name: Ultrasound Normal Kidney Image
full_name: Ultrasound Normal Kidney Image Computer Vision Dataset
notes: Roboflow v1 contains 1,080 images, all assigned to the training set, with no preprocessing or augmentation reported. Although the project name emphasizes normal kidney imaging, the released segmentation classes also include liver and spleen; the atlas therefore records this entry under multi-anatomy with Abdomen as the primary anatomy and Kidney, Liver, and Spleen as targets. The label "Normal-Kidney" is preserved as a released segmentation class rather than interpreted as a separate anatomical organ. Patient count, acquisition institution, equipment, selection criteria, and source provenance are not documented. During verification, page metadata were available through search indexing, but direct archive access was blocked by Cloudflare; verification is therefore marked partial.

name: GIST514-DB
full_name: GIST514-DB
paper_title: Query2: Query over Queries for Improving Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumour Detection in an Endoscopic Ultrasound
notes: GIST514-DB contains 514 endoscopic-ultrasound images/cases: 263 gastrointestinal stromal tumors and 251 leiomyomas. Native annotations include class labels, lesion bounding boxes, lesion contours/instance annotations, and anatomical-location information. Endoscopic acquisition is recorded in acquisition.note while the underlying imaging mode is normalized to B-mode.

name: LEPset
full_name: LEPset
notes: LEPset contains 11,500 endoscopic-ultrasound images from 420 patients. The labeled subset contains 3,500 images for pancreatic-cancer versus non-pancreatic-cancer classification, while another 8,000 images are unlabeled. The unlabeled portion is retained as a native pretraining resource rather than encoding self-supervised learning as a separate learning-paradigm task. The Zenodo record is a data resource rather than a dedicated peer-reviewed paper, so paper is set to null.

name: C-TRUS
full_name: C-TRUS
paper_title: C-TRUS: A Novel Dataset and Initial Benchmark for Colon Wall Segmentation in Transabdominal Ultrasound
paper_venue: International Workshop on Advances in Simplifying Medical Ultrasound (ASMUS)
notes: C-TRUS contains 827 transabdominal B-mode ultrasound images extracted from sequences of 13 patients and provides pixel-wise colon-wall masks. Bowel-wall localization and thickness/inflammation quantification can be derived from the masks or used as downstream analyses, but no independent localization or measurement ground-truth annotation is encoded here; segmentation is therefore the only native task.

name: OpticNerveSheaths
full_name: Optic Nerve Sheath Transorbital Ultrasound Images
paper_title: Development of a Deep Learning-Based System for Optic Nerve Characterization in Transorbital Ultrasound Images on a Multicenter Data Set
notes: The current Mendeley release contains 464 transorbital B-mode ultrasound images with multi-annotator optic-nerve/optic-nerve-sheath region and diameter-related annotations. The release year is 2023, and the atlas points to the current Mendeley Data version 2.

name: Ultrasound Elastography Dataset for Unsupervised Training
full_name: Ultrasound Elastography Dataset for Unsupervised Training
paper_title: Semi-supervised Training of Optical Flow Convolutional Neural Networks in Ultrasound Elastography
paper_venue: Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention - MICCAI 2020
notes: This is a 2022 public release of 2,200 paired RF acquisitions from a tissue-mimicking breast phantom. Pair relationships are available, but ground-truth displacement maps, strain maps, segmentation masks, and diagnostic labels are not. Consequently, displacement estimation and optical-flow estimation are downstream unsupervised modeling objectives rather than supervised native annotations. The atlas therefore represents the reusable resource as pretraining and signal-analysis data. Separate in-vivo liver-cancer evaluation data described in associated papers are not established as part of this public release and are excluded. The official page does not state a dataset license or exact reusable train/validation/test counts. The current Dropbox shared-folder archive is about 35.8 GB and was not fully downloaded during verification, so verification is marked partial.

name: Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset
full_name: Regensburg Pediatric Appendicitis Dataset
anatomy_target: Appendix | Right lower quadrant | Intestines | Lymph nodes | Reproductive organs
paper_title: Interpretable and intervenable ultrasonography-based machine learning models for pediatric appendicitis
notes: The public release and the paper represent different stages of the cohort. The spreadsheet contains 782 rows, 760 of which have a non-empty US_Number, while the image archive contains 2,097 files under 707 numeric filename prefixes. Only 579 prefixes link to the current spreadsheet; those matched prefixes contain 1,727 raw images, whereas the paper reports a 579-patient, 1,709-image analysis subset after additional exclusions. These counts are therefore recorded separately rather than merged into a single misleading dataset size. The release contains patient-level diagnosis, management, severity, clinical/laboratory variables, and expert-recorded ultrasonographic findings, but no pixel-level masks or bounding boxes. Multiview learning, image-and-tabular multimodal learning, and concept-bottleneck learning are methodological settings of the associated work rather than additional native dataset tasks.

name: Dermatologic Ultrasound Images for classification
full_name: Dermatologic Ultrasound Images for Classification
paper_title: Discriminative deep learning based benignity/malignancy diagnosis of dermatologic ultrasound skin lesions with pretrained artificial intelligence architecture
notes: This resource is not currently represented elsewhere in the atlas and is suitable for inclusion as a primary medical-ultrasound dataset. The public Kaggle version contains 202 skin-lesion instances, each intended to include paired B-mode and Color Doppler images plus a binary benign/malignant label, a specific diagnosis field (Dx), and transducer-frequency metadata. The associated 2022 paper describes a larger institutional study cohort: 235 histologically confirmed skin-lesion images were used for model development and an additional 35 images for external testing. These paper counts should not be substituted for the 202-instance public Kaggle release. A 2026 study that re-used the Kaggle resource reported several data-quality issues: B-mode/Doppler filenames were inverted for records 57, 59, and 90; filename-format corrections were needed for several other records; and records 6, 62, 74, and 121 contained two Doppler images instead of a proper B-mode/Doppler pair. These issues do not invalidate the dataset but should be considered during preprocessing. A 2025 review of publicly disseminated ultrasound resources independently lists this dataset as an open-access skin-ultrasound dataset with 202 cases. No dataset-specific reusable license could be independently confirmed from the currently retrievable Kaggle metadata, so access.license is left null.
